title: Cap. 7 Theologi nostri open: Postremo — Bucerus on Matt. 1:21 elect
latin: 11. Postremo, Theologi nostri, qui Christum pro omnibus passum non diffitentur, tamen illum in morte sua peculiari quodam intuitu electos redemisse simul profitentur: Bucerus sententiam suam expressit in Math. i. ad illa verba, Populum suum salvum faciet, Hoc est, electos, quos ipsi Pater adducit. Morte sua omnium electorum peccata expiavit, meruitque ut illis Pater propitius suum Spiritum donet. Hic videtis Christum morte sua meruisse aliquid electis quod aliis non meruit. At quicquid cuiquam meruit Christus, id meruit secundum ordinationem & acceptationem Patris sui: Ex Patris igitur voluntate & ordinatione Christi mors pertinet ad electos speciali quadam ratione, sub qua ad alios non extenditur.
pass_a_gloss: 11. Finally, our theologians, who do not deny that Christ suffered for all, yet at the same time profess that he in his death redeemed the elect by a certain peculiar regard: Bucer expressed his opinion on Matthew 1 at those words, He shall save his people — that is, the elect, whom the Father himself brings to him. By his death he expiated the sins of all the elect, and merited that the Father, being propitious, should give them his Spirit. Here you see that Christ by his death merited something for the elect which he did not merit for others. But whatever Christ merited for anyone, he merited according to the ordination and acceptance of his Father: Therefore from the Father's will and ordination Christ's death pertains to the elect by a certain special reason, under which it is not extended to others.
pass_b: 11. Last, our own theologians. They do not deny that Christ suffered for all, yet they also confess that in his death he redeemed the elect under a peculiar regard. Bucer states it on Matthew 1 at He shall save his people — that is, the elect whom the Father himself brings to him. By his death he expiated all the elect's sins and merited that the propitious Father give them his Spirit. So Christ's death merited something for the elect that he did not merit for others. Whatever he merited for anyone, he merited under the Father's ordination and acceptance. From that Fatherly will and ordination, then, Christ's death belongs to the elect in a special way that does not reach the rest.

lemmas.gloss: by a peculiar regard / special view

title: Cap. 7 Theologi nostri: Musculus — electorum gratia Christ came
latin: Musculus, qui in locis communibus acriter illud urget, Christum pro universali Redemtore habendum, tamen specialem Christi intentionem de redimendis electis agnoscit, in Rom. viii. ubi dicit, Electorum gratia Christum in hunc mundum venisse. Quod aliter intelligi non potest, quam peculiari intentione electorum infallibiliter servandorum in mundum venisse. Quae specialis intentio obtinendi ipsis electis fructum applicatum suae passionis est ita illorum propria, ut ad alios se haud extendat.
pass_a_gloss: Musculus, who in his Common Places sharply urges that Christ is to be held as universal Redeemer, yet acknowledges Christ's special intention concerning redeeming the elect, on Romans 8, where he says that Christ came into this world for the sake of the elect. Which cannot be understood otherwise than that he came into the world with a peculiar intention of infallibly saving the elect. Which special intention of obtaining for the elect themselves the applied fruit of his passion is so proper to them that it hardly extends itself to others.
pass_b: Musculus, who in the Common Places presses hard that Christ must be held universal Redeemer, still grants Christ's special intention to redeem the elect. On Romans 8 he says Christ came into this world for the elect's sake — which can only mean he came with a peculiar intention to save the elect without fail. That special aim, securing for the elect the applied fruit of his passion, belongs to them so properly that it does not stretch to others.

lemmas.gloss: for the sake of the elect / by grace of the elect

title: Cap. 7 Theologi nostri: Calvin — Heb. 2 children given; three notes
latin: Calvinus in Hebr. ii. ad illa verba, Ecce ego & pueri quos mihi dedit Deus, Nullos, inquit, adducit Christus ad Patrem, nisi ab ipso sibi datos. Hanc vero donationem ex aeterna electione pendere scimus: quia quos Pater destinavit ad vitam, eos in custodiam Filio suo tradit, ut ipsos tueatur. Tria hic notanda: Primum est, Deum Patrem quosdam ex decreto electionis singulariter ad vitam destinasse: Secundum, Christum Mediatorem hosce electos quasi peculiariter sibi commendatos a Patre accepisse: Tertium, singularem curam horum electorum Christum gerere, eosque ita tueri & regere in hac vita, ut tandem perducat ad aeternam. Quibus positis, ab omni ratione & religione abhorrerer, qui iret inficias, Christum, in ipso opere oblationis suae & redemtionis humanae, horum electorum salutem peculiari intentione, id est, absoluta & efficaci, intendisse.
pass_a_gloss: Calvin on Hebrews 2 at those words, Behold I and the children whom God has given me: Christ, he says, brings none to the Father except those given to him by the Father himself. But we know that this donation hangs upon eternal election: because those whom the Father has destined to life, he hands over into his Son's custody, that he may keep them. Three things are here to be noted: First, that God the Father has singularly destined some to life from the decree of election: Second, that Christ the Mediator has received these elect as it were peculiarly committed to him by the Father: Third, that Christ bears a singular care of these elect, and so keeps and rules them in this life that he at length leads them through to eternal life. Which things having been laid down, I would shrink from all reason and religion from the one who would go about to deny that Christ, in the very work of his oblation and of human redemption, intended the salvation of these elect by a peculiar intention, that is, by an absolute and efficacious one.
pass_b: Calvin on Hebrews 2 at Behold I and the children God has given me: Christ brings none to the Father, he says, except those the Father himself has given him. That gift hangs on eternal election: those the Father destined for life he places in the Son's keeping to guard them. Mark three points. First, the Father from the election decree has singularly destined some for life. Second, Christ the Mediator received those elect as peculiarly entrusted to him by the Father. Third, Christ keeps a singular care of them, guarding and ruling them in this life until he brings them to eternal life. With that set down, it would offend all reason and piety to deny that, in the very work of his offering and of mankind's redemption, Christ intended these elect's salvation by a peculiar intention — absolute and effectual.

title: Cap. 7 Theologi nostri: Zanchius — sufficiently for all, efficaciously for elect
latin: Zanchius, in Miscellaneis, tract. De praedest. san. pag. 14. Falsum non est, Christum mortuum pro omnibus hominibus: Omnibus enim passio Christi offertur in Evangelio. Sed pro electis tantum efficaciter mortuus est: quia scilicet ipsi tantum efficacitatis passionis Christi participes fiunt. Quod autem illi soli fiant participes hujus passionis efficaciter, id referendum est ad specialem & efficacem voluntatem Christi patientis, Deique Patris hanc hostiam acceptantis, pro electis magis peculiari modo quam pro aliis. In boni enim salutiferi participatione voluntas Divina praecedit humanam.
pass_a_gloss: Zanchi, in the Miscellanies, treatise On the Predestination of the Saints, page 14. It is not false that Christ died for all men: for to all the passion of Christ is offered in the Gospel. But he died efficaciously only for the elect: because namely they alone become partakers of the efficacy of Christ's passion. But that they alone become partakers of this passion efficaciously is to be referred to the special and efficacious will of Christ suffering, and of God the Father accepting this victim, for the elect in a more peculiar manner than for others. For in the participation of saving good the Divine will precedes the human.
pass_b: Zanchi (Miscellanies, On the Predestination of the Saints, p. 14): it is not false that Christ died for all men — his passion is offered to all in the Gospel. Yet he died efficaciously only for the elect, because they alone share the passion's efficacy. That they alone so share it must be referred to the special, effectual will of Christ suffering and of the Father accepting this victim — for the elect in a more peculiar way than for others. In sharing saving good, the divine will goes before the human.

lemmas.gloss: the divine will precedes the human

title: Cap. 7 Theologi nostri: Vorstius — Amica duplic peculiar redemption sense
latin: Denique, ne taedio sim plures autores congerendo, Vorstius ipse non potuit negare, redemtionem in cruce peractam peculiari quadam ratione ad electos pertinere. Sic enim loquitur, in Amica duplic. pag. 230, Constat redemtionis vocem diverso sensu ad plures ejusdem generis species aptari posse; ac proinde aliquos tantum, & non omnes, quadam speciali ratione seu peculiari sensu redemtos dici commode posse, inque sacris literis sic appellari solere. Idem, pag. 235. respondens loco adducto ex Heb. xiii. 20, in quo Christus magnus Pastor ovium per sanguinem foederis aeterni appellatur, concedit nobis, Christum esse harum ovium, & quidem harum tantum, Pastorem peculiari modo, puta quoad salvificam & spiritualem illas pascendi actum, qui actualem Spiritus sancti donationem continet, item quoad specialem quandam harum ovium acquisitionem. Hactenus ille.
pass_a_gloss: Finally, lest I be tedious by heaping up more authors, Vorstius himself could not deny that the redemption accomplished on the cross pertains to the elect by a certain peculiar reason. For thus he speaks, in the Friendly Duplicate, page 230: It is agreed that the word redemption can be fitted in a diverse sense to several species of the same genus; and therefore that some only, and not all, can conveniently be said to have been redeemed by a certain special reason or peculiar sense, and are accustomed to be so called in the sacred writings. The same, page 235, answering the place brought from Hebrews 13:20, in which Christ is called the great Shepherd of the sheep through the blood of the eternal covenant, concedes to us that Christ is the Shepherd of these sheep, and indeed of these alone, in a peculiar manner, namely as to the saving and spiritual act of feeding them, which contains the actual donation of the Holy Spirit, and likewise as to a certain special acquisition of these sheep. Thus far he.
pass_b: Finally — not to weary by stacking more writers — even Vorstius could not deny that the redemption finished on the cross belongs to the elect in a peculiar sense. In the Friendly Duplicate (p. 230) he grants that redemption can be taken in different senses for several species of the same kind, so that some only, not all, may fitly be called redeemed in a special reason or peculiar sense, as Scripture often names them. On p. 235, answering Hebrews 13:20 (Christ the great Shepherd of the sheep through the blood of the eternal covenant), he concedes Christ is Shepherd of these sheep, and of these alone, in a peculiar way: as to the saving, spiritual act of feeding them (which includes the actual gift of the Holy Spirit), and as to a special acquisition of those sheep. So far Vorstius.

title: Cap. 7 Theologi nostri close: Vorstius critique — Bridegroom/Head/Shepherd intent
latin: Quaero quid hoc sit quod nobis Vorstius largitur, quando dat, non omnes sed aliquos speciali ratione & peculiari sensu fuisse morte Christi redemtos; quando ait Christum esse ovium suarum Pastorem peculiari modo, & quoad specialem quandam acquisitionem. Si nihil aliud vult, quam in ipso eventu, pro diversis actibus voluntatum humanarum, fructum redemtionis ad aliquos, hoc est, ad credentes, speciali & peculiari modo pertinere, nugas agit, & testimoniis contra eum allatis omnino non satisfacit. Nam illa omnia, Ecclesiam acquisivit sanguine suo; Dat salutem corpori suo; Animam ponit pro ovibus suis; Mortuus est ut filios Dei congregaret: haec, inquam, & consimilia, non specialem aliquam operationem Ecclesiae, corporis, ovium designant; sed specialem intentionem & operationem sponsi, Capitis, Pastoris circa hanc Ecclesiam, hoc corpus, hasce oves versantis, & eorundem salutem virtute & merito mortis suae speciali voluntate decernentis & procurantis.
pass_a_gloss: I ask what this is that Vorstius grants us, when he grants that not all but some were redeemed by Christ's death by a special reason and peculiar sense; when he says that Christ is the Shepherd of his sheep in a peculiar manner, and as to a certain special acquisition. If he means nothing else than that in the event itself, according to diverse acts of human wills, the fruit of redemption pertains to some, that is, to believers, in a special and peculiar manner, he is trifling, and does not at all satisfy the testimonies brought against him. For all those things — He acquired the Church by his blood; He gives salvation to his body; He lays down his life for his sheep; He died that he might gather the sons of God — these, I say, and the like, do not designate some special operation of the Church, of the body, of the sheep; but the special intention and operation of the bridegroom, the Head, the Shepherd, busied about this Church, this body, these sheep, and by a special will decreeing and procuring their salvation by the virtue and merit of his death.
pass_b: What exactly does Vorstius grant us when he allows that not all but some were redeemed by Christ's death in a special reason and peculiar sense, and that Christ is Shepherd of his sheep in a peculiar way as to a special acquisition? If he means only that, in the outcome, by diverse acts of human wills, redemption's fruit reaches some — that is, believers — in a special way, he trifles and never answers the texts brought against him. For He purchased the Church with his blood; He gives salvation to his body; He lays down his life for his sheep; He died to gather God's children — these and like sayings do not mark some special act of the Church, body, or sheep. They mark the Bridegroom's, Head's, and Shepherd's special intention and work toward this Church, this body, these sheep, decreeing and securing their salvation by his death's virtue and merit under a special will.

lemmas.gloss: He acquired the Church by his blood (Acts 20:28)
